title: BBK BBK Worker Designer return v1
x-bbk-requirements: Return one `bbk.role-return.v1` object with `contract` = `bbk.worker-designer-return.v1`, `role` = `bbk_worker_designer`, an allowed `invocation_mode`, an allowed `return_kind`, an allowed `operational_disposition`, and `semantic_state.name` = `invocation_design_state` with an allowed `semantic_state.value`. Do not substitute prose, a generic status word, or a legacy handoff disposition for these exact discriminators.

A new Worker invocation contract must not emit or accept `READY_FOR_VALIDATION` as its current result state. Use an active operational disposition and a separate semantic execution state; preserve a legacy handoff value only as historical input and require current parent-owned candidate-admission evidence.

Use `READY_FOR_PARENT_INTEGRATION` only for one current concrete Worker invocation contract whose WorkUnit is semantically complete; effective model, profiles, skills, context, tools, authority, capabilities, workspace requirements, assurance, budget, continuation, result, cleanup and handoff are exact; required static qualification passes; and any remaining dynamic binding is explicitly permitted and non-blocking.

Use `READY_AS_REUSABLE_TEMPLATE` only for a deliberately requested non-authorizing template. It may define a maximum qualified pattern but must not carry a live subject, workspace lease, credential, candidate identity, standing authority instance or evidence claim, and it must require per-instance narrowing and preflight.

Use `NEEDS_RUNTIME_BINDING` when the host-neutral design is complete but a live workspace lease, session, credential handle, endpoint, device, scheduler or other dynamic binding is owned by the runtime or orchestrator. This state is not a technical failure and grants no permission to fabricate the binding.

Permissions and scopes always intersect and narrow; mandatory Worker obligations, assurances and safeguards union. A profile, skill, tool, model or host capability can never broaden the accepted authority or canonical `bbk_worker` envelope.

Preserve schema truth. When current WorkUnit or other canonical schemas cannot represent a required invocation detail—especially non-filesystem capabilities—use a named companion artifact bound by the Worker Designer return and handoff instead of adding unsupported fields or pretending the detail is unnecessary.

A valid Worker invocation contract or template means only that the physical execution envelope is ready for parent integration or later runtime binding. It does not mean the Worker was launched, execution was authorized, the WorkUnit completed, a candidate was frozen or valid, a finding was closed, risk was accepted, or release was granted.

The effective Worker has no child-agent authority and may not own independent review, validation, approval, user interaction or cross-territory integration. Any such need returns to the parent for a different canonical role or topology.

Host-specific projections must preserve the host-neutral contract's role, authority, tools, context, skills, effects, budgets, result and handoff semantics. Audit-only metadata belongs in manifests or projection headers that are not injected as model instructions unless behavior depends on it.

The `result` object must contain every field declared by the role result schema. Use an empty collection or null only where the field schema permits it and record the reason in the corresponding structured value.
This return is governed by `spec/contracts/catalog.json`, the common `bbk.role-return.v1` envelope, and the role-specific return and result schemas named by this contract.
x-bbk-readiness-rule: `READY_FOR_PARENT_INTEGRATION` may be returned only when every current input, required role-owned output, blocking dependency, evidence carrier, cleanup obligation, invalidation condition, and durable handoff required by this contract has been reconciled. The state authorizes only the next parent integration or assessment step named by the role contract.
x-bbk-authority-boundary: A valid `bbk.worker-designer-return.v1` return establishes only the `bbk_worker_designer`-owned result for the exact subject, parent, invocation mode, and attempt. It cannot create human authority, broaden execution permission, silently assume another canonical role, erase findings or failed attempts, accept risk, approve an operating baseline, authorize deployment or publication, establish outcome achievement, or grant release except where a separate accountable authority and contract explicitly establish that effect.
